proposal.title: Split uncompressed sample chunks into latitude bands for parallel full-field reads
proposal.hypothesis: Operational evidence shows the consumer benchmark is warm-cache shuffled full-field tensor access over 28 samples, and provider/cache download changes cannot improve it. The current uncompressed one-sample full-spatial chunks minimize decompression but leave each channel read as one large chunk task. If each published data array keeps one time sample per chunk but splits the latitude axis into two contiguous bands, a full-field tensor sample can be assembled from smaller independent uncompressed chunk reads that xarray/zarr/dask may schedule with more parallelism and lower per-task copy latency. This should increase consumer_samples_per_second while preserving all frozen array paths, coordinates, selector dimensions, validation, Zarr v3 consolidated policy, provenance, rerun behavior, dependencies, and the public pipeline interface.
proposal.expected_tradeoffs: Chunk object count and metadata may increase, and materialization may do more chunk writes. Output bytes should remain approximately unchanged because chunks stay uncompressed float32 payloads, though per-chunk headers may add a small footprint increase.

edits.rationale: Keeps the proven uncompressed one-sample time chunking but splits only the latitude dimension into two contiguous chunks to test whether more independent warm-cache chunk tasks improve full-field sample throughput.

proposal.validation_plan: Rerun the evaluator and compare consumer_samples_per_second against node_0003 while confirming contract_correctness, semantic_equivalence, rerun_safety, and provenance_security remain passing and frozen channel/coordinate paths are unchanged.
